questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $P = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$, $M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$, $N = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & 10 \\ -3 & 10 \end{pmatrix}$ and $PM = N$. Find $PM$ in terms of $a$ and $b$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Multiply row by column:

$PM = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ -1 & 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2a + 3(-1) & 2b + 3(2) \\ a + 4(-1) & b + 4(2) \end{pmatrix}$

$PM = \begin{pmatrix} 2a - 3 & 2b + 6 \\ a - 4 & b + 8 \end{pmatrix}$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the values of $a$ and $b$. *[6 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Since $PM = N$, equate corresponding entries:

$2a - 3 = -1 \Rightarrow 2a = 2 \Rightarrow a = 1$

$2b + 6 = 10 \Rightarrow 2b = 4 \Rightarrow b = 2$

Check with the second row: $a - 4 = 1 - 4 = -3$ and $b + 8 = 2 + 8 = 10$. Both agree with $N$.

**Answer: $a = 1$ and $b = 2$.**
